reason: Neither conversation found the sensible step of checking the front-accessible cartridge fuse in the fused spur, and both leaned on an unsupported 'control board / mains input fuse' diagnosis. Conversation 1 was worse on safety and listening: it twice told a self-declared non-competent homeowner to remove the spur faceplate (which still has live incoming conductors with only the switch off), repeated a socket test for a hardwired unit after being told there was no socket, and ignored the customer's direct question about a spur fuse, though its final electrician-then-engineer routing was clear. Conversation 2 obtained the make and model, kept its one hands-on check behind the isolated spur switch (kickplate, power off), and respected the customer's stated limits, but its final reply trailed off into speculation about the PCB without a firm escalation and included odd advice like 'unplug it' for a hardwired machine, so it wins only narrowly.
